rationale: The Court is likely to adopt a McNeill-inflected, backward-looking rule fixing the CSA-schedule comparator at the time of the prior state conviction to avoid making ACCA predicates turn on later federal rescheduling. Sotomayor (possibly joined by Jackson) is the most likely dissenter emphasizing temporal silence, fairness, and lenity, while Gorsuch/Thomas are the most likely to add a short concurrence about executive rescheduling and the absence of grievous ambiguity.
